correctness.rationale: The target in RESULT.md line 5 is J=integral_0^1 X(t) dt, whereas lines 36–40 use the Itô kernel for X(1)=integral_0^1 B(t) dt. Stochastic Fubini gives J=integral_0^1 (1-u)^2/2 dB(u), variance 1/20, and covariances with (X(z),B(z)) equal to (z^2(6-4z+z^2)/24, z(3-3z+z^2)/6). The observation covariance K is as given, but the target covariance is not. Thus both the risk and the optimizing design fail, not merely a normalization of the displayed risk. For P=10 the claimed optimal risk 1/14 exceeds the risk 1/20 of ignoring all data. For an exact design counterexample at that budget, both designs use z=1, where the true c=(1/8,1/6). The proposed (p,q)=(8,2) yields reduction c^T(K+diag(1/8,1/2))^(-1)c=53/1512, whereas (p,q)=(10,0) yields (1/8)^2/(1/3+1/10)=15/416, an improvement of 79/78624. Separately, even noiseless observations leave residual risk at least z^5/720+(1-z)^5/20: the quadratic part on [0,z] cannot be represented by an affine function, and the tail is unobserved. The minimum of this bound on [0,1] is positive, unlike the claimed limit. The source checker fixes the wrong c at line 13 and integrates f=1-xx at lines 54–60, so its reported PASS in VERIFICATION.md does not address this discrepancy. Inspected but did not run check.py. No repaired theorem for the stated target is claimed.

value.rationale: The measurement-budget question is worthwhile, but the delivered result supplies no sharp law for that question: its central risk formula and optimal allocation are false for the advertised integrated-Wiener functional. The surviving fixed-design Gaussian reduction after correcting c and the coefficient-to-precision Cauchy–Schwarz rule are standard. A switch theorem for X(1) would instead concern prediction of a terminal path value (equivalently the integral of B), and substituting that different target is not an established result about integration of X. No separate repaired finding is submitted.
